offence_severity: Minimum punishment of 07 years for Section 376 IPC
number_of_offences: Three offences charged (328, 354, 376 IPC), all upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the scientific investigation of mobile phone call details and medical reports to establish the falsity of the prosecutrix's allegations.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly the prosecutrix, as credible only if their statements were supported by scientific evidence, otherwise deemed false.
trial_duration: Offence dates: 15.2.2007, 23.12.2006, 25.12.2006, 1.1.2007; Trial judgment: 1.12.2008; High Court decision: 16.1.2009; Supreme Court decision: 23.1.2013
legal_representation: K.T.S. Tulsi, Gaurave Bhargava (for appellant); R.K. Rathore, Vikas Bansal, D.S. Mahra (for respondent)
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed on 28.6.2007; charges framed on 1.12.2008; FIR quashed by High Court on 27.8.2007; charge-sheet quashed by Supreme Court
appeal_history: Trial court: charges framed; High Court: dismissed revision petition; Supreme Court: appeal allowed, criminal proceedings quashed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the complainant/prosecutrix's statements led to the registration of an FIR and the filing of a charge-sheet against the appellant-accused for offences punishable under Sections 328, 354, and 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the complainant/prosecutrix's allegations were false, as evidenced by mobile phone call details, her marital status, and the lack of scientific evidence to substantiate the charges against the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the High Court has inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash criminal proceedings if the material produced by the accused is sound, reasonable, and indubitable, and would lead to the conclusion that the prosecution's case is false.
precedent_relied_upon: Gajraj vs. State (NCT) of Delhi 2011 (12) SCR 701; Rajiv Thaper & Ors. vs. Madan Lal Kapoor (2013] 1 SCR
